title: From Complex Workflows to Reusable Product Systems
subtitle: Data-heavy B2B interaction, AI-first prototyping, and shared patterns that help teams ship

cv.note: Tailored for the (Senior) Product Designer - Systems & AI role

bio.short: I turn complex, domain-specific workflows into usable tools and repeatable product capabilities. At Datameer, I designed data-dense analytics for regulated banks and insurers. ChurchDesk and Ninox add reusable operational workflows, no-code systems, and AI-generated output that stays editable. Today I build working prototypes and cross-platform design infrastructure with AI coding agents.
bio.long:
At Datameer, I led UX for an enterprise analytics platform used in regulated banking and insurance. The work covered query builders, big-data pivot tables, aggregated JSON views, filters, and uncertainty in sampled previews. I brought research into roadmap decisions for a new platform and defined design-system component behavior and specifications while UI created the visual system.

At ChurchDesk, I owned product management for the main platform and led product design across the company. I reframed a funeral-booking brief as a reusable capability inside the calendar and form builder customers already used. Coordination fell from days to hours: about 70% by my estimate. Booking acceptance reached 90%. At Ninox, I owned the design system. I later designed prompt-to-database onboarding in which generated schemas appear in the real editor beside chat and remain directly editable.

Today at Bibel TV, I prototype product concepts in working code against production APIs. AI coding agents shorten the path from evidence to implementation. I also built a four-tier token system and served API that keep Android, web, and Figma aligned. The Packmatic throughline is concrete: learn the work, identify the repeatable interaction model, and build a system that users and engineers can rely on.

context.company: Packmatic builds data-based packaging-management software for specifications, supplier collaboration, compliance, cost, and sustainability workflows.
context.role: A hands-on systems and AI product-design role spanning research, data-heavy B2B workflows, reusable UX patterns, design-system stewardship, working prototypes, and implementation collaboration.
context.emphasis: Lead with data-heavy interaction design and reusable workflow capabilities, then show the current AI-first prototyping practice and the design-system bridge into engineering.
